crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Credit Scoring with Alternative Data
children.blurb: Credit scoring with alternative data covers the use of nontraditional records, such as rent, utility, telecom, cash flow, and public records, to estimate repayment risk when traditional bureau files are thin or stale.

children.name: Covenant Extraction
children.blurb: Covenant extraction is the work of turning the terms of credit agreements, indentures, and loan documents into structured data that a credit team can query and monitor.

children.name: Predicting Distress and Default
children.blurb: Predicting distress and default covers the estimation of a borrower's or issuer's likelihood of failing to meet debt obligations over horizons set by the portfolio or regulatory context.

children.name: Modelling the Yield Curve
children.blurb: Modelling the yield curve covers the estimation of the term structure of interest rates from market prices, including spot rates, forward rates, discount factors and par yields.

children.name: Stress Testing Structured Credit
children.blurb: Stress testing structured credit covers securitized products such as RMBS, CMBS, ABS, CLOs and CDOs, and the tranches that sit on top of underlying pools.

sections.body: Fixed income and credit risk covers the lending and bond markets, where the main questions are whether a borrower will pay back and what happens if they do not. Artificial intelligence is now used to score borrowers using alternative data such as rent payments, utility bills, and cash flow records, which can extend credit to people without traditional credit histories. In covenant extraction, natural language processing reads loan agreements and indentures to pull out financial ratios, negative pledges, and event of default triggers. Distress prediction models combine accounting data, market prices, and news text to estimate the probability that a company will default or enter bankruptcy. Yield curve modelling uses machine learning to fit the term structure of interest rates and to forecast how it might shift under different economic conditions. Stress testing structured credit applies AI to simulate losses on pools of mortgages, auto loans, and credit card receivables under adverse scenarios.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Credit scoring with alternative data is deployed in some consumer lending, but regulators in many jurisdictions still require explainable models, which limits complex black box approaches. Covenant extraction has improved with transformer based language models, yet legal language is ambiguous and rare clauses still cause errors. Distress prediction achieves useful accuracy on historical data, but it struggles with sudden regime changes, like a pandemic or a sharp rate hike, because the past may not resemble the future. Yield curve modelling can fit historical curves well, but forecasting turning points in monetary policy remains unreliable. Stress testing structured credit faces model risk, data gaps, and the challenge of calibrating correlations during crises. The honest limits are that AI does not remove the need for judgment, and many models are only as good as the data and assumptions behind them.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from individual loans to portfolio level risk. Credit Scoring with Alternative Data is the starting point for assessing a single borrower's likelihood of repayment. Covenant Extraction then reads the legal terms that constrain that borrower and trigger consequences if ratios or payments slip. Predicting Distress and Default moves from a single borrower to a company or issuer, estimating the chance of failure over a horizon. Modelling the Yield Curve supplies the discount rates and macro context that connect credit spreads to broader interest rate movements. Stress Testing Structured Credit brings these threads together for securitized pools, where many loans are bundled and tested against recessions or market shocks. The site's 222 compliance and regulation pages provide background on the rules that shape covenants and the reporting standards that stress tests must follow.
